summary: Routing policies editor: snapshot restore applies stale SLA/route flags causing mismatched active rules
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled snapshot restore of historical routing policies into the staging config-store, the routing policies editor surface continued to show the pre-restore (newer) rule set while the serving runtime and reporting pipelines started enforcing the restored (older) rules.

Impact:
- Customer-facing routing mismatches: requests served under incorrect routing policies for ~22 minutes in us-east.
- SLA enforcement flags (priority escalation macros) reverted to older values leading to unexpected quota throttles and at least one P1 customer support escalation.
- Reporting and analytics showed dropped metrics for the newer rule IDs because the serving runtime used the restored snapshot IDs.

Environment:
- prod/us-east (primary config-store cluster), routing-editor v3.8.1, config-store (consul) cluster 3.2.0, rule-engine v2.4.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger a snapshot restore via the console snapshot UI (selected historic snapshot created 2026-03-08T02:00Z).
2) Simultaneously have two engineers editing routing rule drafts in the editor (autosave enabled).
3) The restore applied to the backend config-store. Serving runtime pulled the restored snapshot on next poll (~30s).
4) Editor UI kept rendering the in-memory draft / cached policy (user-facing preview) until autosave conflict resolution completed, creating a divergent persisted policy state.

Observed behavior:
- Serving runtime enforced restored snapshot rules immediately after its poll.
- Editor preview showed newer draft rules and allowed publish attempts that failed with a 409 because the active config had a lower sequence ID.
- Reporting pipelines ingested events tagged with restored rule IDs, causing customer-facing dashboards to show mismatched rule exposures.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot restore should acquire a global apply lock or otherwise quiesce editor autosaves until restore completes so editor preview matches persisted active rules.
- Publish attempts during restore should surface a clear blocking error and not permit conflicting drafts to be published without sequence reconciliation.

Logs / artifacts:
- Serving logs (rule-engine): "applied_snapshot id=20260308-02:00 sequence=1124" (2026-03-09T13:04:06Z),
- Editor client console trace: "cache-miss -> rendering draft(seq=1130)" (2026-03-09T13:04:12Z),
- Config-store events: restore job logs (config-store restore-id=restore-20260308-0200, duration=18s)",
- Reporting sample: dashboard spike showing ruleset change at 2026-03-09T13:04:20Z (link: https://observability.redwood/reports/route-diff/46290)",
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Priya): Correlation of timestamps shows the restore completed ~6s before serving runtime poll but editor autosave/draft machinery continued to present a newer sequence. Hypothesis: snapshot restore does not currently set a 'restore-in-progress' coordination flag in the config-store, so editor and runtime can diverge briefly.

SRE (Diego): Pulled consul event stream; found race between 'apply_snapshot' and per-editor autosave reconcile job. Editor reconcile attempts attempt a blind merge when sequence mismatch occurs, which can leave an in-memory display different from persisted state until user refresh.

Rule-engine team: Confirmed serving runtime correctly applies the persisted snapshot; however, analytic tagging uses rule-name -> id mapping cached by routing-ui service which was not invalidated by restore, causing reporting pipeline to backfill with older IDs.

Security/QA: No unauthorized changes detected; restore request came from a scheduled operator job (not automated third-party).

Root cause (working): Lack of a coordinated restore-lock and stale cache invalidation between editor UI, config-store restore paths, and reporting ingestion. There's a missing step that marks a 'restore_in_progress' key and forces editor to show a blocking banner and prevents drafts from being published until reconcile completes.
comments: 2026-03-09 13:30 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Captured consul event stream and increased restore logging. I reproduced locally by running concurrent editor autosave and restore job. Filing follow-up: add global apply lock and editor-side blocking UX.

2026-03-09 14:10 - Maya Chen (Rule-engine): Confirmed runtime behavior; will add an immediate cache-bust RPC on snapshot apply to reporting ingestion workers. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-engine/pull/2314
2026-03-09 15:05 - Priya Nair (Support Ops): Customer notified internally; we advised temporary mitigation (manual publish after verify). Customer CS case SUP-8824 linked for visibility.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Patch candidate prepared to set 'restore_in_progress' key and block editor publish attempts. Need code review from @Maya and @Liam.

2026-03-12 11:43 - Liam O'Connor (Frontend): UX banner for 'Restore in progress' implemented and feature-flagged; client will disable publish and surface a clear message. QA flagged one flaky scenario where autosave attempted a silent merge; fixed in client-side reconcile logic. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-ui/pull/942
resolution_notes:
Temporary workaround implemented (2026-03-09): instruct ops to run restore during a maintenance window and to notify editor users to refresh; manual verification checklist added to Route Snapshot Runbook.

Fix rollout (in progress as of 2026-03-13):
- Backend: config-store PR to set/clear a 'restore_in_progress' coordination key during snapshot apply (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/config-store/pull/782).
- Frontend: feature-flagged banner and publish-block changes merged to staging (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-ui/pull/942).
- Runtime: added immediate cache-bust notification to reporting ingestion on snapshot apply (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-engine/pull/2314).

Post-deploy follow-ups (assigned):
- Add e2e test that runs concurrent autosave + snapshot restore to prevent regressions (owner: QA, ticket INT-46810).
- Create alert when serving/runtime sequence != editor/latest-seq for > 30s (owner: Observability, ticket INT-46812).
- Update runbook to include manual restore verification steps and communication checklist (owner: Support OPS).

Status: patch set merged to canary; monitoring in place. Planned full rollout after 48h canary observation if no anomalies.
next_steps: 1) Complete canary rollout and monitor the alert for sequence divergence for 48h. 2) Close linked customer cases after confirmation from CS. 3) Convert feature-flag for UX blocking into default once backend lock is in stable release. 4) Document the snapshot/restore coordination pattern in the Rule Engine design doc.
resolution_status: Fix in progress; workaround and runbook updated; monitoring set.
